## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Anekavaṇṇavimānavatthu* (Vv 82, also designated Vv 7.8) belongs to the *Vimānavatthu* in the Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral; Radich 2007]. In this text, a celestial youth (*deva*) explains to Mahā-Moggallāna that he attained his splendid celestial rebirth through the merit of encouraging others to revere the relics (*dhātu*) of the past Buddha Sumedha following that Buddha's *parinirvāṇa* [SuttaCentral; Radich 2007].
In modern scholarship on Buddhist somatic and devotional traditions, the text is cited alongside other *Vimānavatthu* narratives as canonical evidence for early relic veneration, illustrating how exhorting companions to pay homage to the relics of an enlightened being was held to secure a heavenly rebirth [Radich 2007].
No cross-language parallels in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan are recorded on SuttaCentral or identified by DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, DharmaNexus identifies extensive Pali-internal text reuse with 15 other Pali texts (82 matches), most prominently with the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (48 matches, spanning §4.1–8.4). It also shares standard recurring verse formulas with numerous other poems in the collection, such as *Gopālavimānavatthu* (Vv 80, §2.5–5.1 ↔ §3.3–6.1), *Paṭhamaagāriyavimānavatthu* (Vv 65), *Paṭhamapatibbatāvimānavatthu* (Vv 11), *Cittalatāvimānavatthu* (Vv 75), and *Sunikkhittavimānavatthu* (Vv 85) [DharmaNexus].
